content.title: Chicago Fire FC dig deep, defeat Philadelphia Union 2-1 on the road
content.text: The win is the Fire’s first over Philadelphia on the road since the 2013 MLS season There weren’t many pretty moments but the Chicago Fire did just enough to take three points back home from Pennsylvania. The Fire defeated the Philadelphia Union 2-1 on Saturday afternoon at Subaru Park in Chester thanks to goals on each side of halftime from Chicago Fire Designated Players Hugo Cuypers and Jonathan Bamba, respectively. The win is the Fire’s first on the road over Philadelphia since August 3, 2013. Chicago started out on the back foot and things only went further downhill when Philip Zinckernagel had to be removed from the match in the 31st minute after a clash of heads that left the Fire’s 2025 MLS All-Star worse for wear. Those issues only compounded themselves when the Union nearly scored in the 35th minute but Alejandro Bedoya’s effort rang off the crossbar, sparing Chicago from an early deficit. The Fire took the lead in the third minute of first half stoppage time and it was thanks to Andrew Gutman, who was making his season debut at left back after missing Chicago’s first four games of 2026. Robin Lod’s pass from midfield was deflected right to Gutman on the left wing and the left back immediately made a run into Philadelphia’s penalty area. Gutman dragged multiple defenders towards him before hitting a cross that the unmarked Hugo Cuypers headed easily into the Union’s goal, giving the Fire the lead for a few moments. Chicago couldn’t hold onto that lead for long and Philadelphia was able to equalize before halftime.Story continues below. Frankie Westfield had a throw in from the left wing that was headed onto the far post by Alejandro Bedoya for Milan Iloski, who scored from close-range to tie the match before the break after the Fire completely switched off defensively. Something changed after halftime for the Chicago Fire as they were a much stronger side and were able to hold on after scoring the match-winning goal in the 58th minute. Robin Lod had the ball on the right side of the Union’s penalty area in the 58th minute and floated a cross over the head of Hugo Cuypers, which was enough to drag Nathan Harriel away from Jonathan Bamba long enough for the Fire’s winger to score from close-range to put his side up with a half hour remaining. The Fire looked like they were going to go up by two in the 83rd minute after Bamba made a great run down the left wing but Lod’s finish bounced off the crossbar to ensure the match finished 2-1 in Chicago’s favor. It wasn’t the prettiest of performances from the Fire but head coach and director of football Gregg Berhalter was impressed by his side’s resilience in a tough environment on the road. “You had to earn the right to play today,” Berhalter said. “Philly is very aggressive against the ball. They close you down very quickly. They thrive on first and second balls, and it took at least 35 minutes to get there. “I thought the end of the first half was exactly how we wanted to start playing, and we did and we got the goal. And you know, unfortunate goal to give up on a strange play but the guys didn’t waiver. They stayed resolute and they stuck to the game plan, and you know, strong second half. And then at the end, just proud of the group for the way they fought and held together under some pressure.” There was a sense of relief throughout the Fire’s locker room after they finally defeated the Union on the road. “It’s been a long time since we got one here against them, huh?” Chicago Fire goalkeeper Chris Brady said. “Yeah, the motto all week was just ‘embrace the duel, embrace the battle,’ because we knew that’s kind of what they feed off of. I think that the guys were great about that today, and I’m just happy we got the three points. We really needed it, especially after last year.” Andrew Gutman got the assist on the Fire’s first goal of the game in his first appearance of the season after getting hurt during warmups ahead of Chicago’s final preseason match. Gutman’s inclusion in the squad made everyone around him more confident entering the game. “I know he was excited to get back, he was itching to get back out there and I’m happy to see him out there as well,” Brady said. “His presence, especially on the offensive side of the ball was slightly missed and it does help having a guy like that, a veteran guy who is not afraid to whip in a good ball. Yeah, happy to see him back and performing well.” Starting 11: Chris Brady (GK), Andrew Gutman, Mbekezeli Mbokazi, Joel Waterman, Leonardo Barroso, Dje D’Avilla, Anton Salétros, Robin Lod, Philip Zinckernagel, Jonathan Bamba, Hugo Cuypers Substitution at 31’: Maren Haile-Selassie on for Philip Zinckernagel Substitution at 46’: Viktor Radojevic on for Andrew Gutman Substitution at 89’: Jason Shokalook and Jonathan Dean on for Robin Lod and Jonathan Bamba Unused Subs: Jeff Gal (C), Jack Sandmeyer, Mauricio Pineda, Sergio Oregel Jr., Attendance: 18,753
